The Punjab, or Panjab (“five rivers”), is a region in South Asia that includes territories of north India and eastern Pakistan. In India, Punjab includes Punjab state, Chandigarh territory, Haryana, and parts of Rajasthan, Jammu Division, Himachal Pradesh and Delhi. In Pakistan, Punjab includes the Punjab province and parts of Azad Kashmir and the Islamabad Capital Territory. The name Punjab means “the land of five waters,” which refers to the Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas and Sutlej Rivers, all of which are tributaries of the Indus River.
Major cities in Punjab include:

*   Lahore (Punjab, Pakistan): population 10.5 million. Lahore is Pakistan’s second largest metropolitan area and the most abundant native Punjabi-populated city in the world. It’s also one of the world’s most densely populated cities.  
*   Faisalabad (Punjab, Pakistan): population: 5.28 million. Faisalabad is the third-largest metropolis in Pakistan and a famous industrial city.  
*   Rawalpindi (Punjab, Pakistan): population 3.25 million. Commonly called Pindi, the city is located 9 miles from Islamabad, and it’s the 4th most populous urban area in Pakistan.  
*   Multan (Punjab, Pakistan): 2.6 million.  
*   Guijranwala (Punjab, Pakistan): 2.57 million.  
*   Ludhiana (Punjab, India): 1.6 million.  
*   Faridabad (Haryana, India): 1.4 million.  
*   Amritsar (Punjab, India): 1.18 million.  
*   Islamabad (Islamabad Capital Territory, Pakistan): 1.15 million.  
*   Chandigarh (Chandigarh, India): 960,000.

## Punjab Demographics
Modern Punjabis are mostly a mix of Indo-Scythian and Indo-Aryan people, with smaller amounts of Semitic ancestry. Indo-Scythians refers to Scythians (or Sakas), Iranian equestrian tribes who migrated into central and northern South Asia during the 2nd century BC to the 4th century AD.
The rise of Islam also brought many settlers from Kashmir, Arabia, Uzbekistan, Turkmenistan, Afghanistan and Mongolia into the area. Today, most Punjab is made up of Dalits, Arains, Ahirs, Gujjars, Jatts, Khatris, Rajputs and Maliks.
Punjabi is the primary language of the region, with several dialects spoken. The majority of Pakistani Punjabis are Sunni Muslim, with minorities that include Ahmadi Muslim, Shia Muslim, and Christians. In Indian Punjab, Hindus and Sikhs are the majority. Nearly 60% of the Indian Punjab population in Sikh, followed by 37% Hindu, while the rest are Jains, Muslims, and Christians.
The size of each state/province in Punjab with estimated populations are:
Punjab, India: 21 million (60% Sikhs, 35% Hindus, 2% Muslims) Haryana, India: 18 million (90% Hindus) Himachal Pradesh, India: 5.5 million (96% Hindus) Punjab, Pakistan: 80 million (95% Muslims)

## History of Punjab
Punjab is today home to many religions and ethnic groups due to a long history of invasions. It was also the home of one of the earliest known South Asia cultures, the Harappa, in prehistoric times. In 326 BCE, Alexander the Great invaded the tip of Punjab near present-day Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, defeating King Porus. His armies then entered the rest of the region with a rule up to modern-day Sialkot, Pakistan. The Maurya Empire ruled the area starting in 305 BCE and for many generations before it was consolidated into the Indo-Greek Kingdom in 180 BCE.
Between 711 and 713 CE, 18-year-old Arab Sultan Muhammad bin Qasim came to the region to defeat Raja Dahir, conquering the Sindh and Punjab areas and bringing Islam to the region for the first time. Muslim empires then ruled Punjab for nearly 1,000 years.
In 1748, the formation of the Dal Khalsa at Amritsar led to the division of the region in 36 areas and 12 separate Sikh principalities. It was then that the start of a Punjabi Sikh Empire began. 22 of the 36 regions were united by Maharaja Ranjit Singh, with the other 14 accepting British sovereignty. Six years later, the British East India Company declared war and, after, two wars, Punjab was annexed by the British.
Partition in 1947 led to the region being split into East and West Punjab, with East Punjab becoming part of India while West Punjab became part of Pakistan.

## Detailed Solution
ShareDownload Solution PDF
The correct answer is **Ludhiana**.   
**Key Points**
*   **Ludhiana** is the largest city in the state of **Punjab** both in terms of area and **population**.  
*   According to the **Census of India 2011**, the population of Ludhiana city was approximately **1,618,879**, making it the most populous urban center in the state.  
*   It is centrally located on the **Grand Trunk Road** (NH 44) and is famously known as the **Manchester of India** due to its massive **textile** and **hosiery** industry.  
*   The city serves as a major industrial hub, particularly for **bicycle manufacturing**, **sewing machines**, and **auto-parts**, which attracts a large migrant workforce from across the country.  
*   The **Ludhiana district** itself is the most populated district in Punjab, housing nearly **12.6%** of the state's total population as per 2011 data.
**Additional Information**
*   **Pathankot**:   
    *   Situated at the meeting point of **Punjab**, **Himachal Pradesh**, and **Jammu and Kashmir**, it serves as a strategic **military base** and a gateway to the hills, but its population is significantly lower than industrial cities like Ludhiana.

*   **Hoshiarpur**:   
    *   Known as the **City of Saints**, it is famous for its **ivory inlay work** and **woodwork**. It has a high **literacy rate** but remains a medium-sized city in terms of demographic scale.

*   **Muktsar** (Sri Muktsar Sahib):   
    *   A city of great **historical and religious significance** in Sikhism, known for the **Battle of Muktsar** (1705). It is primarily an **agricultural** and administrative center with a relatively smaller urban population.

*   **Other Major Cities**: After Ludhiana, **Amritsar** and **Jalandhar** are the next most populous cities in Punjab, serving as major cultural and surgical/sports goods hubs respectively.

ShareDownload Solution PDF
The correct answer is **Ludhiana**.   
**Key Points**
*   **Ludhiana** is the largest city in the state of **Punjab** both in terms of area and **population**.  
*   According to the **Census of India 2011**, the population of Ludhiana city was approximately **1,618,879**, making it the most populous urban center in the state.  
*   It is centrally located on the **Grand Trunk Road** (NH 44) and is famously known as the **Manchester of India** due to its massive **textile** and **hosiery** industry.  
*   The city serves as a major industrial hub, particularly for **bicycle manufacturing**, **sewing machines**, and **auto-parts**, which attracts a large migrant workforce from across the country.  
*   The **Ludhiana district** itself is the most populated district in Punjab, housing nearly **12.6%** of the state's total population as per 2011 data.
**Additional Information**
*   **Pathankot**:   
    *   Situated at the meeting point of **Punjab**, **Himachal Pradesh**, and **Jammu and Kashmir**, it serves as a strategic **military base** and a gateway to the hills, but its population is significantly lower than industrial cities like Ludhiana.

*   **Hoshiarpur**:   
    *   Known as the **City of Saints**, it is famous for its **ivory inlay work** and **woodwork**. It has a high **literacy rate** but remains a medium-sized city in terms of demographic scale.

*   **Muktsar** (Sri Muktsar Sahib):   
    *   A city of great **historical and religious significance** in Sikhism, known for the **Battle of Muktsar** (1705). It is primarily an **agricultural** and administrative center with a relatively smaller urban population.

*   **Other Major Cities**: After Ludhiana, **Amritsar** and **Jalandhar** are the next most populous cities in Punjab, serving as major cultural and surgical/sports goods hubs respectively.

Climate is not uniform over the whole region, as the areas adjacent to the Himalayas generally receive heavier rainfall than those at a distance.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab#cite_note-114) The Köppen climate classification generally classifies Punjab as having either a monsoon-influenced humid subtropical climate (Köppen: Cwa) or a hot semi-arid climate (Köppen: BSh).

The transitional period after the monsoon season is cool and mild, leading to the winter season, when the temperature in January falls to 5°C (41°F) at night and 12°C (54°F) by day. After Ranjit Singh's death in 1839, the empire was severely weakened by internal divisions and political mismanagement. This opportunity was used by the East India Company to launch the First and Second Anglo-Sikh Wars. The country was finally annexed and dissolved at the end of the Second Anglo-Sikh War in 1849 into separate princely states and the province of Punjab. Eventually, a Lieutenant Governorship was formed in Lahore as a direct representative of the Crown.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab#cite_note-hibb_1980-88):221
In British India, until the Partition of India in 1947, the Punjab Province was geographically a triangular tract of country of which the Indus River and its tributary the Sutlej formed the two sides up to their confluence, the base of the triangle in the north being the Lower Himalayan Range between those two rivers. Moreover, the province as constituted under British rule also included a large tract outside these boundaries. Along the northern border, Himalayan ranges divided it from Kashmir and Tibet. On the west it was separated from the North-West Frontier Province by the Indus, until it reached the border of Dera Ghazi Khan District, which was divided from Baluchistan by the Sulaiman Range. To the south lay Sindh and Rajputana, while on the east the rivers Jumna and Tons separated it from the United Provinces.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjab#cite_note-Chisholm_1911,_p._653-111) In total Punjab had an area of approximately 357 000 km square about the same size as modern day Germany, being one of the largest provinces of the British Raj.
Map of the Punjab Province (British India)

In 1901 the frontier districts beyond the Indus were separated from Punjab and made into a new province: the North-West Frontier Province. **Ludhiana** (Panjabi: _Ludhiāṇā_, pronounced[[lʊ́d̪͜tɪ̀ɪˈäːɳäː]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Punjabi "Help:IPA/Punjabi")) is the most populous city in the Indian state of Punjab.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-164.100.161.224-11) The city has an estimated population of 1,618,879 as of the2011 census and distributed over 310 km 2 (120 sq mi),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-District-6) making Ludhiana the most densely populated urban centre in the state.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-12) It is a major industrial centre of Northern India, referred to as "India's Manchester" by the BBC.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-13) It is also known as the commercial capital of Punjab.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-164.100.161.224-11)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-15)
It stands on the old bank of Sutlej River, that is now 13 kilometres (8.1 mi) to the south of its present course. The Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has placed Ludhiana on the 48th position among the top 100 smart cities,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-16) and the city has been ranked as one of the easiest cities in India for business according to the World Bank.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-17)

Although the area around present-day Ludhiana had been inhabited since ancient times, the modern city was established during the late fifteenth century under the Lodi dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. Prior to its foundation, the region comprised several agricultural settlements located along the southern bank of the Sutlej River, whose course has since shifted further north.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-ludhiana.nic.in-18)
During the rule of the Tughlaq dynasty, a fort was constructed to protect the strategic route linking Delhi with north-western India. The fort was captured by the Khokhar ruler Jasrat during his campaign in Punjab in 1421–22, illustrating the declining authority of the Delhi Sultanate in the region.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-19)
Ludhiana was founded in 1480 during the reign of the Lodi dynasty.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-Britannica-20) According to tradition, Sultan Sikandar Lodi sent two military commanders, Yusuf Khan and Nihad Khan, to restore Lodi authority in Punjab. While Yusuf Khan crossed the Sutlej River and established Sultanpur Lodhi, Nihad Khan founded Ludhiana at the village of Mir Hota.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-21).
The city's name was originally _Lodi-ana_, meaning "the town of the Lodis", which gradually evolved into _Lodiana_ and eventually _Ludhiana_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-ludhiana.nic.in-18)
The Lodhi Fort, popularly known as _Purana Qila_, is the only surviving monument from the city's foundation. It was repaired during the reign of Maharaja Ranjit Singh and later maintained by the British administration before falling into disrepair after independence. In December 2013, it was declared a state-protected monument by the Government of Punjab.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-22)

As Punjab's largest industrial and manufacturing centre, Ludhiana has experienced significant in-migration from other parts of India, particularly Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh. ### Partition and post-independence
Punjabi, written in the Gurmukhi script, is the official language of Punjab and is the principal language of administration, education and local governance in Ludhiana. English is widely used for higher education, judicial proceedings, business and official correspondence, while Hindi is commonly understood and spoken throughout the city owing to its diverse population.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-53)
The municipal administration of Ludhiana began with the establishment of the Municipal Council in 1870. Following the Partition of India in 1947, the city gained strategic importance because of its central location in the reorganised Punjab and emerged as a major industrial centre. Following rapid population growth and urban expansion, the Municipal Corporation of Ludhiana was constituted in 1976 under the Punjab Municipal Act, 1976, replacing the earlier municipal council.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-54) It corporation is responsible for the provision and maintenance of civic infrastructure and public services, including roads, street lighting, water supply, sewerage, sanitation, solid waste management, public health, parks, and urban planning.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-Hindustan_Times_23_July_2021-55)
The administration of the Ludhiana Municipal Corporation is headed by the Municipal Commissioner, Mr. Ojasvi Alankar, IAS.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-56) The Corporation governs an area of 159.37 km² (61.53 sq mi)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-Website-1-57)

Ludhiana is represented in the Lok Sabha by the Ludhiana Lok Sabha constituency, one of the 13 parliamentary constituencies in Punjab. The constituency comprises six assembly constituencies located entirely within the city. Since the 2024 Indian general election, it has been represented by Amrinder Singh Raja Warring of the Indian National Congress, who defeated Ravneet Singh Bittu of the Bharatiya Janata Party by 20,942 votes.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-59)

As Punjab's largest city by population and one of northern India's principal industrial centres, Ludhiana plays a significant role in the state's politics. Ludhiana produces 60% of India's tractor parts and a large portion of auto and two-wheeler parts. **Ludhiana** (Panjabi: _Ludhiāṇā_, pronounced[[lʊ́d̪͜tɪ̀ɪˈäːɳäː]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Punjabi "Help:IPA/Punjabi")) is the most populous city in the Indian state of Punjab.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-164.100.161.224-11) The city has an estimated population of 1,618,879 as of the2011 census and distributed over 310 km 2 (120 sq mi),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-District-6) making Ludhiana the most densely populated urban centre in the state.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-12) It is a major industrial centre of Northern India, referred to as "India's Manchester" by the BBC.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-13) It is also known as the commercial capital of Punjab.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-164.100.161.224-11)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-15)
It stands on the old bank of Sutlej River, that is now 13 kilometres (8.1 mi) to the south of its present course. The Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has placed Ludhiana on the 48th position among the top 100 smart cities,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-16) and the city has been ranked as one of the easiest cities in India for business according to the World Bank.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-17)
texts.4:
Although the area around present-day Ludhiana had been inhabited since ancient times, the modern city was established during the late fifteenth century under the Lodi dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. Prior to its foundation, the region comprised several agricultural settlements located along the southern bank of the Sutlej River, whose course has since shifted further north.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-ludhiana.nic.in-18)
During the rule of the Tughlaq dynasty, a fort was constructed to protect the strategic route linking Delhi with north-western India. The fort was captured by the Khokhar ruler Jasrat during his campaign in Punjab in 1421–22, illustrating the declining authority of the Delhi Sultanate in the region.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-19)
Ludhiana was founded in 1480 during the reign of the Lodi dynasty.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-Britannica-20) According to tradition, Sultan Sikandar Lodi sent two military commanders, Yusuf Khan and Nihad Khan, to restore Lodi authority in Punjab. While Yusuf Khan crossed the Sutlej River and established Sultanpur Lodhi, Nihad Khan founded Ludhiana at the village of Mir Hota.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-21).
The city's name was originally _Lodi-ana_, meaning "the town of the Lodis", which gradually evolved into _Lodiana_ and eventually _Ludhiana_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-ludhiana.nic.in-18)
The Lodhi Fort, popularly known as _Purana Qila_, is the only surviving monument from the city's foundation. It was repaired during the reign of Maharaja Ranjit Singh and later maintained by the British administration before falling into disrepair after independence. In December 2013, it was declared a state-protected monument by the Government of Punjab.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-22)

### Partition and post-independence
Punjabi, written in the Gurmukhi script, is the official language of Punjab and is the principal language of administration, education and local governance in Ludhiana. English is widely used for higher education, judicial proceedings, business and official correspondence, while Hindi is commonly understood and spoken throughout the city owing to its diverse population.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-53)
The municipal administration of Ludhiana began with the establishment of the Municipal Council in 1870. Following the Partition of India in 1947, the city gained strategic importance because of its central location in the reorganised Punjab and emerged as a major industrial centre. Following rapid population growth and urban expansion, the Municipal Corporation of Ludhiana was constituted in 1976 under the Punjab Municipal Act, 1976, replacing the earlier municipal council.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-54) It corporation is responsible for the provision and maintenance of civic infrastructure and public services, including roads, street lighting, water supply, sewerage, sanitation, solid waste management, public health, parks, and urban planning.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-Hindustan_Times_23_July_2021-55)
The administration of the Ludhiana Municipal Corporation is headed by the Municipal Commissioner, Mr. Ojasvi Alankar, IAS.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-56) The Corporation governs an area of 159.37 km² (61.53 sq mi)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-Website-1-57)

**Ludhiana** (Panjabi: _Ludhiāṇā_, pronounced[[lʊ́d̪͜tɪ̀ɪˈäːɳäː]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Punjabi "Help:IPA/Punjabi")) is the most populous city in the Indian state of Punjab.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-164.100.161.224-11) The city has an estimated population of 1,618,879 as of the2011 census and distributed over 310 km 2 (120 sq mi),[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-District-6) making Ludhiana the most densely populated urban centre in the state.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-12) It is a major industrial centre of Northern India, referred to as "India's Manchester" by the BBC.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-13) It is also known as the commercial capital of Punjab.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-164.100.161.224-11)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-15)
It stands on the old bank of Sutlej River, that is now 13 kilometres (8.1 mi) to the south of its present course. The Union Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs has placed Ludhiana on the 48th position among the top 100 smart cities,[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-16) and the city has been ranked as one of the easiest cities in India for business according to the World Bank.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-17)

Although the area around present-day Ludhiana had been inhabited since ancient times, the modern city was established during the late fifteenth century under the Lodi dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate. Prior to its foundation, the region comprised several agricultural settlements located along the southern bank of the Sutlej River, whose course has since shifted further north.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-ludhiana.nic.in-18)
During the rule of the Tughlaq dynasty, a fort was constructed to protect the strategic route linking Delhi with north-western India. The fort was captured by the Khokhar ruler Jasrat during his campaign in Punjab in 1421–22, illustrating the declining authority of the Delhi Sultanate in the region.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-19)
Ludhiana was founded in 1480 during the reign of the Lodi dynasty.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-Britannica-20) According to tradition, Sultan Sikandar Lodi sent two military commanders, Yusuf Khan and Nihad Khan, to restore Lodi authority in Punjab. While Yusuf Khan crossed the Sutlej River and established Sultanpur Lodhi, Nihad Khan founded Ludhiana at the village of Mir Hota.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-21).
The city's name was originally _Lodi-ana_, meaning "the town of the Lodis", which gradually evolved into _Lodiana_ and eventually _Ludhiana_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-ludhiana.nic.in-18)
The Lodhi Fort, popularly known as _Purana Qila_, is the only surviving monument from the city's foundation. It was repaired during the reign of Maharaja Ranjit Singh and later maintained by the British administration before falling into disrepair after independence. In December 2013, it was declared a state-protected monument by the Government of Punjab.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ludhiana#cite_note-22)
